name: AquaSense-ICS
description: AquaSense-ICS: a hybrid real-simulated cyber-physical dataset and leakage-aware benchmark for smart water quality monitoring and attack detection Machine-learning research on water cyber-physical systems is constrained by datasets that are either real but chemically poor, or simulated but free of sensing noise and attacks. AquaSense-ICS co-registers, on a common elapsed-time axis: Real edge recording: a 25.4 h window (8.0 h of recorded data, 31.5% coverage, 23 gaps longer than 60 s) from a Raspberry Pi 5 node with a TDS probe and a Bosch BME680 ambient sensor (temperature, relative humidity, gas resistance), sampled every 1-2 s (23,688 records). EPANET-MSX simulation: a looped network of 13 nodes (10 junctions, 2 reservoirs, 1 tank) simulated for 24 h, with six water-quality species (chlorine, pH, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, trihalomethanes) and one wall species, plus two pulse injections (chlorine at J3, turbidity at J7). Attack and fault library: a seeded generator of five cyber-attack types (false data injection, stealthy FDI, replay, denial of service, drift) and three unintentional sensor faults (white noise, spikes, extreme values), with sample-level ground truth. Augmented and TimeGAN-generated sequences, released in separate files and flagged by the origin column in the fused table. They are intended for training only.
